text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay B opens with a clear claim that driverless cars 'aren't as reliable as a regular car and will ultimately cause more crashes,' then develops this position throughout.", "quality": "Clear thesis and sustained focus", "description": "Essay B states a precise, arguable position up front and consistently develops that single argument across the essay."}, {"evidence": "Essay B reasons through scenarios like drivers on phones, system glitches, and cars unable to handle issues, connecting each to crash risk.", "quality": "Developed reasoning with causal logic", "description": "Essay B builds its case through extended cause-and-effect reasoning rather than asserting points without elaboration."}, {"evidence": "Essay B acknowledges the appeal of not driving ('it would be nice to not have to worry about doing all the work') before rebutting it.", "quality": "Counterargument acknowledgment", "description": "Essay B concedes a point in favor of driverless cars and then addresses why the risks outweigh that benefit, strengthening its persuasiveness."}, {"evidence": "Essay B has a proper introduction, body paragraphs, and a conclusion that returns to its thesis and offers an alternative solution.", "quality": "Structured organization", "description": "Essay B follows a clear argumentative structure with a distinct introduction, developed body, and concluding recommendation."}, {"evidence": "Essay B maintains a consistent, controlled tone and avoids the informal phrasing and digressions present in Essay A.", "quality": "Consistent formal register", "description": "Essay B sustains a more controlled and polished voice appropriate to argumentative writing."}]}
